author: Diamond Sutra Detailed Explanation
excerpt: Homage to Śākyamuni Buddha, our original teacher (recited three times)

inline.s: Homage to Śākyamuni Buddha, our original teacher
(recited three times)

blocks.text: The Opening Verse

inline.s: The Dharma, supremely profound and subtle,
Is hard to encounter in hundreds of millions of aeons.
I now see, hear, and earnestly receive it;
May I realize the true meaning of the Tathagata.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Kumarajiva of the Later Qin.

blocks.text: Part One: The Gatherings and Causes of the Assembly

inline.s: Thus have I heard. At one time the Buddha was dwelling in the Jetavana Grove, the park of Anathapindada of Shravasti, together with a great assembly of bhikshus numbering twelve hundred and fifty.

At that time, when it was mealtime, the World-Honored One put on his robe and took up his bowl, and entered the great city of Shravasti to beg for alms. Having begged in succession within the city, he returned to the place of his abode. When the meal was over, he laid aside his robe and bowl, washed his feet, arranged his seat, and sat down.

blocks.text: Part Two: The Request of the Elder Subhuti

inline.s: Then the elder Subhuti rose from his seat amid the assembly, bared his right shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, pressed his palms together respectfully, and addressed the Buddha: Rare, World-Honored One, is the Tathagata who protects and remembers the bodhisattvas well, and who well commands the bodhisattvas.
World-Honored One! When good men and good women resolve their minds upon anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, how should they abide? How should they subdue their minds?

The Buddha said: Good, good. Subhuti, as you have said, the Tathagata protects and remembers the bodhisattvas well, and well commands the bodhisattvas. Listen now with care, and I shall speak it for you.
When good men and good women resolve their minds upon anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, they should thus abide and thus subdue their minds. So be it, World-Honored One. I wish to hear it.

blocks.text: Part Three: The Great Vehicle, the True Doctrine

inline.s: The Buddha told Subhuti: All the bodhisattvas-mahasattvas should thus subdue their minds. All of every kind of living being — whether born from eggs, born from wombs, born from moisture, or born by transformation; whether endowed with form or without form; whether with thought, without thought, or neither with thought nor without thought — I shall cause them all to enter nirvāṇa without remainder and be led to extinction. Yet when thus immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless living beings are led to extinction, in truth there is no living being that is led to extinction.
Why is this? Subhuti, if a bodhisattva has the mark of self, the mark of a person, the mark of a being, or the mark of a lifespan, he is not a bodhisattva.

blocks.text: Part Four: Wondrous Conduct Without Abiding

inline.s: Furthermore, Subhuti, a bodhisattva should not abide anywhere when giving: he should give not abiding in form, not abiding in sound, smell, taste, touch, or dharma. Subhuti, a bodhisattva should thus give without abiding in marks. Why? If a bodhisattva gives without abiding in marks, his merit is immeasurable.

Subhuti, what do you think? Can the space in the east be measured? No, World-Honored One. Subhuti, can the space in the south, west, north, the four quarters, and above and below, be measured? No, World-Honored One. Subhuti, when a bodhisattva gives without abiding in marks, his merit is likewise inconceasurable, immeasurable. Subhuti, a bodhisattva should abide only as thus taught.

blocks.text: Part Five: Seeing Truth As It Really Is

inline.s: Subhuti, what do you think? Can the Tathagata be seen by means of his physical body? No, World-Honored One. The Tathagata cannot be seen by means of his physical body. Why? Because what the Tathagata speaks of as the physical body is not the physical body.
The Buddha told Subhuti: All forms are utterly false and delusive. If you see that all forms are non-forms, then you will see the Tathagata.

blocks.text: Part Six: Rare Right Faith

inline.s: Subhuti addressed the Buddha: World-Honored One, will there be living beings who, hearing these words and phrases, will give rise to true faith? The Buddha told Subhuti: Do not speak thus. After the Tathagata has passed away, in the last five hundred years, there will be those who hold precepts and cultivate merit who, upon these words and phrases, will be able to give rise to faith and accept them as true.

Know that such persons planted roots of good not merely under one Buddha, two, three, four, or five Buddhas, but have planted roots of good under immeasurable thousands of myriads of kotis of Buddhas. Those who hear these words and phrases and give rise even to a single thought of pure faith — Subhuti, the Tathagata knows and sees them all; these living beings obtain thus immeasurable merit.

Why? Because these living beings no longer have the mark of self, the mark of a person, the mark of a being, or the mark of a lifespan; they have no mark of a dharma, and also no mark of a non-dharma.

Why? Because if these living beings take up a mark in their minds, they are attached to self, person, being, and lifespan. If they take up the mark of a dharma, they are attached to self, person, being, and lifespan. Why? If they take up the mark of a non-dharma, they are attached to self, person, being, and lifespan. Therefore one should not take up a dharma, and should not take up a non-dharma.
For this reason the Tathagata always says: You bhikshus, know that the Dharma I speak is like a raft; even the Dharma should be abandoned, how much the more so the non-Dharma.

blocks.text: Part Seven: No Attainment, No Teaching

inline.s: Subhuti, what do you think? Has the Tathagata attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi? Has the Tathagata expounded a dharma? Subhuti said: As I understand the meaning of what the Buddha has spoken, there is no fixed dharma called anuttara-samyak-sambodhi; nor is there any fixed dharma that the Tathagata can expound.

Why? The dharma the Tathagata has expounded can neither be grasped nor spoken. It is neither a dharma nor a non-dharma. How is this? All sages and worthy ones differ only by virtue of the unconditioned Dharma.

blocks.text: Part Eight: Born From the Dharma

inline.s: Subhuti, what do you think? If a person filled the three thousand great thousand worlds with the seven treasures and used them for giving, would this person's merit be great? Subhuti said: Very great, World-Honored One. Why? Because this merit is not the nature of merit; therefore the Tathagata speaks of it as great merit.

If, on the other hand, a person receives and holds even a four-line gatha from this sutra and speaks it for others, his merit surpasses that. Why? Subhuti, all Buddhas, and the anuttara-samyak-sambodhi Dharma of all Buddhas, are born from this sutra.
Subhuti, what is called Buddha and Dharma is not Buddha and Dharma; therefore it is called Buddha and Dharma.

blocks.text: Part Nine: One Marklessness

inline.s: Subhuti, what do you think? Can a srotapanna think, ‘I have attained the fruit of srotapanna’? Subhuti said: No, World-Honored One. Why? Because srotapanna means ‘one who has entered the stream,’ yet he has entered nothing; he has not entered form, sound, smell, taste, touch, or dharma. Thus he is called a srotapanna.

Subhuti, what do you think? Can a sakridagamin think, ‘I have attained the fruit of sakridagamin’? Subhuti said: No, World-Honored One. Why? Because sakridagamin means ‘one who returns once more,’ yet in truth there is no returning; therefore he is called a sakridagamin.

Subhuti, what do you think? Can an anagamin think, ‘I have attained the fruit of anagamin’? Subhuti said: No, World-Honored One. Why? Because anagamin means ‘one who does not return,’ yet in truth there is no not-returning; therefore he is called an anagamin.

Subhuti, what do you think? Can an arhat think, ‘I have attained the way of the arhat’? Subhuti said: No, World-Honored One. Why? Because in truth there is no dharma called arhat. World-Honored One, if an arhat were to think, ‘I have attained the way of the arhat,’ he would be attached to self, person, being, and lifespan.

World-Honored One, the Buddha said that I have attained the samādhi of non-contention and am the foremost among men, the first arhat free from desire. World-Honored One, I do not think, ‘I am an arhat free from desire.’ World-Honored One, if I were to think, ‘I have attained the way of the arhat,’ then the World-Honored One would not have said that Subhuti delights in the practice of the quiet retreat. Because Subhuti in truth practices nothing, therefore he is called ‘one who delights in the practice of the quiet retreat.’

blocks.text: Part Ten: Adorning the Pure Land

inline.s: The Buddha told Subhuti: What do you think? When the Tathagata was formerly with Dipankara Buddha, did he attain any dharma? No, World-Honored One. When the Tathagata was with Dipankara Buddha, in truth he attained nothing.
Subhuti, what do you think? Do the bodhisattvas adorn the Buddha-lands? No, World-Honored One. Why? Because that which adorns the Buddha-land is not an adornment; therefore it is called an adornment.

Therefore, Subhuti, all the bodhisattvas-mahasattvas should thus give rise to a pure mind: they should not give rise to a mind abiding in form, nor arise a mind abiding in sound, smell, taste, touch, or dharma; they should give rise to a mind that abides nowhere.

Subhuti, suppose there were a person whose body were like King Sumeru. What do you think? Is this body great? Subhuti said: Very great, World-Honored One. Why? Because what the Buddha speaks of as the non-body is called the great body.

blocks.text: Part Eleven: The Supremacy of Unconditioned Merit

inline.s: Subhuti, if there were as many Ganges rivers as there are grains of sand in the Ganges, what do you think? Would the sands of all those Ganges rivers be many? Subhuti said: Very many, World-Honored One. These Ganges rivers alone are already countless, how much more their sands.

Subhuti, I shall now tell you truthfully. If a good man or good woman filled the three thousand great thousand worlds with the seven treasures for as many as the sand-grains of all those Ganges rivers, and used them for giving, would he gain much merit? Subhuti said: Very much, World-Honored One.
The Buddha told Subhuti: If a good man or good woman holds and recites even a four-line gatha from this sutra and speaks it for others, this merit surpasses the former merit.

blocks.text: Part Twelve: Honoring the True Teaching

inline.s: Furthermore, Subhuti, wherever this sutra is expounded, even a four-line gatha, know that within that place all the worlds with their devas, humans, and asuras should make offerings, as if it were a Buddha stupa or temple. How much more so if a person is able to receive and hold it completely and recite it.
Subhuti, know that such a person achieves the most supreme and first rarest of dharmas. Wherever this sutra dwells, there is the Buddha, and there too the communities of worthy disciples.

blocks.text: Part Thirteen: Receiving and Holding the Dharma

inline.s: At that time Subhuti addressed the Buddha: World-Honored One, by what name shall this sutra be called? How should we hold and practice it? The Buddha told Subhuti: This sutra is called the Diamond Prajnaparamita. By that name you should hold and practice it.
Why is this? Subhuti, what the Buddha speaks of as the Prajnaparamita is not the Prajnaparamita; therefore it is called the Prajnaparamita.
Subhuti, what do you think? Has the Tathagata expounded any dharma? Subhuti addressed the Buddha: World-Honored One, the Tathagata has shown nothing to be spoken.
Subhuti, what do you think? Of all the atoms of dust in the three thousand great thousand worlds, are they many? Subhuti said: Very many, World-Honored One.
Subhuti, the Tathagata speaks of atoms of dust as not atoms of dust; therefore they are called atoms of dust. The Tathagata speaks of worlds as not worlds; therefore they are called worlds.

Subhuti, what do you think? Can the Tathagata be seen by means of the thirty-two marks? No, World-Honored One. The Tathagata cannot be seen by means of the thirty-two marks. Why? Because what the Tathagata speaks of as the thirty-two marks is not marks; therefore it is called the thirty-two marks.

Subhuti, if a good man or good woman sacrificed his body and life as many times as the sands of the Ganges; and if another person received and held even a four-line gatha from this sutra and spoke it for others, his merit would be far greater.

blocks.text: Part Fourteen: Serene Extinction Through Separation From Marks

inline.s: At that time Subhuti, upon hearing this sutra, deeply understood its meaning, and with tears streaming and sorrowful weeping, addressed the Buddha: Rare, World-Honored One! The Buddha has spoken such a profound sutra; since of old I have possessed the eye of wisdom, yet I have never heard such a sutra as this.

World-Honored One, if a person hears this sutra and his faith is pure, he gives rise to the real form. Know that such a person achieves the first and rarest merit. World-Honored One, this real form is not a form; therefore the Tathagata calls it the real form.

World-Honored One, now that I have heard such a sutra and believe, understand, and receive it, it is not difficult. But in a future age, in the last five hundred years, if living beings hear this sutra and believe, understand, and receive it, they will be the first and rarest.

Why? Because such a person has no mark of self, no mark of person, no mark of being, no mark of lifespan. How is this? The mark of self is not a mark; the mark of person, being, and lifespan are likewise not marks. Why? Because one who is separated from all marks is called a Buddha.
Thus, thus. If again a person hears this sutra and is not startled, not alarmed, not afraid, know that such a person is exceedingly rare.
Why? Subhuti, the Tathagata speaks of the first paramita as not the first paramita; therefore it is called the first paramita.
Subhuti, the paramita of patience — the Tathagata speaks of it as not the paramita of patience; therefore it is called the paramita of patience.

Why? Subhuti, when in former times the king Kalinga cut my body apart, at that time I had no mark of self, no mark of person, no mark of being, no mark of lifespan. Why? Because at the time I was dismembered limb by limb, if I had had the mark of self, the mark of person, the mark of being, or the mark of lifespan, anger and hatred would have arisen.
Subhuti, I also recall that in the past, for five hundred lives, I was an ascetic of patience; throughout those lives I had no mark of self, no mark of person, no mark of being, no mark of lifespan.
Therefore, Subhuti, a bodhisattva should be separated from all marks and give rise to the mind of anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.

He should not arise a mind abiding in form, nor arise a mind abiding in sound, smell, taste, touch, or dharma; he should give rise to a mind that abides nowhere. If the mind abides, it is no abiding. Therefore the Buddha says that the mind of a bodhisattva should not abide in form when giving. Subhuti, for the sake of benefiting all living beings, a bodhisattva should give in this manner.
The Tathagata says that all forms are non-forms. Again he says that all living beings are not living beings.
Subhuti, the Tathagata is a speaker of truth, a speaker of reality, a speaker of suchness, a speaker of non-deceit, a speaker of non-difference.
Subhuti, the Dharma the Tathagata has attained is neither real nor unreal.

Subhuti, if a bodhisattva gives while his mind abides in a dharma, it is as if a man entered into darkness and saw nothing. If a bodhisattva gives while his mind does not abide in a dharma, it is as if a man with eyes, bright with the sunlight, saw all kinds of forms.

Subhuti, in the age to come, if good men and good women are able to receive, hold, and recite this sutra, then the Tathagata, with his Buddha-wisdom, will know and see such persons, and they will all achieve immeasurable and boundless merit.

blocks.text: Part Fifteen: The Merit of Upholding the Sutra

inline.s: Subhuti, if good men and good women gave up their bodies as many as the sands of the Ganges in the morning, again gave up their bodies as many as the sands of the Ganges at midday, and again gave up their bodies as many as the sands of the Ganges in the evening; and if in this manner, for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of myriads of kotis of aeons, they gave up their bodies; and if another person, hearing this sutra, did not reject it with his faith, his merit would surpass theirs. How much more so the merit of one who copies it, receives and holds it, recites it, and expounds it for others.

Subhuti, to sum up, this sutra possesses merit that is inconceivable, incommensurable, and boundless. The Tathagata has spoken it for those who set forth in the Great Vehicle, for those who set forth in the Supreme Vehicle.

If a person is able to receive, hold, and recite it, and broadly expound it for others, the Tathagata will know such a person and see him, and he will achieve merit that is immeasurable, incommensurable, boundless, and inconceivable. Such a person thus bears on his shoulders the Tathagata’s anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.
Why? Subhuti, those who delight in lesser dharmas, being attached to the view of self, person, being, and lifespan, are unable to hear, receive, and recite this sutra, nor to expound it for others.

Subhuti, wherever this sutra is found, all the worlds, their devas, humans, and asuras, should make offerings. Know that this place is a stupa. All should respectfully worship, circumambulate, and scatter flowers and incense upon it.

blocks.text: Part Sixteen: Purifying Karmic Obstacles

inline.s: Furthermore, Subhuti, if good men and good women receive, hold, and recite this sutra, yet are despised by others, it is because the karmic offenses of their former lives should have cast them into the evil paths. But because in this present life they are despised, the karmic offenses of their former lives are thereby dissolved, and they shall attain anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.

Subhuti, I recall that in the past, in immeasurable asamkhyeya aeons, before Dipankara Buddha, I met and respectfully served and offered to eighty-four hundred thousand myriads of nayutas of Buddhas, without missing a single one. If another person, in the last age, is able to receive, hold, and recite this sutra, the merit he obtains will not be one-hundredth, not one-thousandth, not one-myriadth of it — nor can number or simile ever reach it.

Subhuti, if good men and good women, in the last age, receive, hold, and recite this sutra, and I were to tell in full of the merit they obtain, some who heard it would be driven mad, their minds confused, and would be full of doubt and disbelief. Subhuti, know that the meaning of this sutra is inconceivable, and its retribution likewise is inconceivable.

blocks.text: Part Seventeen: Ultimate No-Self

inline.s: At that time Subhuti addressed the Buddha: World-Honored One, when good men and good women resolve their minds upon anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, how should they abide? How should they subdue their minds?

The Buddha told Subhuti: A good man or good woman who resolves his mind upon anuttara-samyak-sambodhi should give rise to this mind: I shall lead all living beings to extinction; and when all living beings are led to extinction, in truth there is no living being who is led to extinction.
Why is this? Subhuti, in truth there is no dharma by which a mind is resolved upon anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.

Subhuti, what do you think? When the Tathagata was with Dipankara Buddha, did he attain anuttara-samyak-sambodhi through any dharma? No, World-Honored One. As I understand the meaning of what the Buddha has spoken, the Buddha, with Dipankara Buddha, attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi through no dharma.

The Buddha said: Even so, even so. Subhuti, in truth there is no dharma by which the Tathagata attains anuttara-samyak-sambodhi. Subhuti, if there were a dharma by which the Tathagata attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, then Dipankara Buddha would not have bestowed upon me the prophecy: ‘In a future life you shall become a Buddha, named Śākyamuni.’ Because in truth there is no dharma by which anuttara-samyak-sambodhi is attained, therefore Dipankara Buddha bestowed upon me the prophecy, saying: ‘In a life to come you shall become a Buddha, named Śākyamuni.’
Why? ‘Tathagata’ means that all dharmas are thus, the principle of thusness.

If someone says the Tathagata attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, Subhuti, in truth there is no dharma by which the Buddha attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi. Subhuti, the anuttara-samyak-sambodhi attained by the Tathagata is in it neither real nor unreal.
Therefore the Tathagata says that all dharmas are Buddha-dharmas. Subhuti, what is called all dharmas is not all dharmas; therefore it is called all dharmas.

Subhuti, it is like a person whose body is great and long. Subhuti said: World-Honored One, what the Tathagata speaks of as the great and long body is not the great body; therefore it is called the great body.

Subhuti, a bodhisattva is also thus. If he says, ‘I shall lead immeasurable living beings to extinction,’ he is not called a bodhisattva. Why? Subhuti, in truth there is no dharma called bodhisattva. Therefore the Buddha says that all dharmas are without self, without person, without being, without lifespan.

Subhuti, if a bodhisattva says, ‘I shall adorn the Buddha-land,’ he is not called a bodhisattva. Why? What the Tathagata speaks of as adorning the Buddha-land is not an adornment; therefore it is called an adornment. Subhuti, a bodhisattva who is fully versed in the dharma of no-self is called by the Tathagata a true bodhisattva.

blocks.text: Part Eighteen: One Body, One Perception

inline.s: Subhuti, what do you think? Does the Tathagata have the fleshly eye? Even so, World-Honored One, the Tathagata has the fleshly eye.
Subhuti, what do you think? Does the Tathagata have the heavenly eye? Even so, World-Honored One, the Tathagata has the heavenly eye.
Subhuti, what do you think? Does the Tathagata have the eye of wisdom? Even so, World-Honored One, the Tathagata has the eye of wisdom.
Subhuti, what do you think? Does the Tathagata have the eye of the Dharma? Even so, World-Honored One, the Tathagata has the eye of the Dharma.
Subhuti, what do you think? Does the Tathagata have the Buddha eye? Even so, World-Honored One, the Tathagata has the Buddha eye.
Subhuti, what do you think? Of all the sands in the Ganges, does the Buddha say they are sands? Even so, World-Honored One, the Tathagata says they are sands.

Subhuti, what do you think? If there were Ganges rivers for each of the sands in one Ganges, and there were Buddha-worlds for all the sands of all those Ganges rivers, would they be many? Very many, World-Honored One. The Buddha told Subhuti: In all those lands, all the living beings, with their manifold minds, the Tathagata knows them all.
Why? Because the Tathagata speaks of all minds as not minds; therefore they are called minds.
How is this? Subhuti, the past mind is unattainable, the present mind is unattainable, and the future mind is unattainable.

blocks.text: Part Nineteen: Universal Transformation of the Dharma Realm

inline.s: Subhuti, what do you think? If a person filled the three thousand great thousand worlds with the seven treasures and used them for giving, would this person, by this cause, gain much merit? Even so, World-Honored One, this person, by this cause, would gain very much merit.
Subhuti, if merit were real, the Tathagata would not speak of gaining much merit; because merit is non-existent, the Tathagata says he gains much merit.

blocks.text: Part Twenty: Leaving Form and Marks

inline.s: Subhuti, what do you think? Can the Buddha be seen as having a complete form body? No, World-Honored One. The Tathagata should not be seen as a complete form body. Why? What the Tathagata speaks of as a complete form body is not a complete form body; therefore it is called a complete form body.

Subhuti, what do you think? Can the Tathagata be seen as complete in all marks? No, World-Honored One. The Tathagata should not be seen as complete in all marks. Why? What the Tathagata speaks of as complete in all marks is not complete; therefore it is called complete in all marks.

blocks.text: Part Twenty-one: What Is Not Spoken Yet Is Spoken

inline.s: Subhuti, do not say that the Tathagata thinks, ‘I shall expound a dharma.’ Do not think thus. Why? If a person says the Tathagata has expounded a dharma, he slanders the Buddha, because he cannot understand what I have spoken. Subhuti, one who expounds the dharma has no dharma to expound; therefore he is called an expounder of the dharma.
At that time the wise Subhuti addressed the Buddha: World-Honored One, will there be living beings in a future age who, hearing this Dharma, give rise to faith?

The Buddha said: Subhuti, they are neither living beings nor not-living-beings. Why? Subhuti, ‘living beings, living beings’ — the Tathagata speaks of them as not living beings; therefore they are called living beings.

blocks.text: Part Twenty-two: No Dharma Attainable

inline.s: Subhuti addressed the Buddha: World-Honored One, has the Buddha’s attainment of anuttara-samyak-sambodhi been no attainment?
The Buddha said: Even so, even so. Subhuti, in anuttara-samyak-sambodhi I have not obtained even the slightest dharma; therefore it is called anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.

blocks.text: Part Twenty-three: Purifying the Mind, Practicing Good

inline.s: Furthermore, Subhuti, this Dharma is equal, with neither high nor low; this is called anuttara-samyak-sambodhi. With no self, no person, no being, no lifespan, and by cultivating all good dharmas, one attains anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.
Subhuti, what are called good dharmas — the Tathagata speaks of them as not good dharmas; therefore they are called good dharmas.

blocks.text: Part Twenty-four: Incomparable Merit and Wisdom

inline.s: Subhuti, if in the three thousand great thousand worlds there were collections of the seven treasures as numerous as all the kings of mountains, Mount Sumeru, and if a person used them for giving; and if another person held, recited, and expounded for others this Prajnaparamita sutra, even a four-line gatha — the former merit would not amount to one-hundredth, one-thousandth, one-hundred-thousandth, one-myriadth of it; nor can number or simile ever reach it.

blocks.text: Part Twenty-five: Transformation With Nothing to Transform

inline.s: Subhuti, what do you think? You should not say that the Tathagata thinks, ‘I shall deliver living beings.’

Subhuti, do not think thus. Why? In truth there are no living beings whom the Tathagata delivers. If there were living beings the Tathagata delivered, then the Tathagata would have self, person, being, and lifespan.
Subhuti, what the Tathagata speaks of as self is not self; yet ordinary people think there is a self.
Subhuti, ordinary people — the Tathagata speaks of them as not ordinary people; therefore they are called ordinary people.

blocks.text: Part Twenty-six: The Dharma Body Has No Marks

inline.s: Subhuti, what do you think? Can the Tathagata be perceived by means of the thirty-two marks? Subhuti said: Even so, even so, the Tathagata is perceived by means of the thirty-two marks.

The Buddha said: Subhuti, if the Tathagata is perceived by means of the thirty-two marks, then a wheel-turning sage king is the Tathagata. Subhuti addressed the Buddha: World-Honored One, as I understand the meaning of what the Buddha has spoken, the Tathagata should not be perceived by means of the thirty-two marks.
At that time the World-Honored One spoke this verse:
If one sees me by means of form, or if one seeks me by means of sound,
That person treads a heterodox path and cannot see the Tathagata.

blocks.text: Part Twenty-seven: Neither Annihilated nor Extinguished

inline.s: Subhuti, if you think the Tathagata attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi because of his complete marks, Subhuti, do not think that the Tathagata attained anuttara-samyak-sambodhi because of his complete marks.

Subhuti, if you think that one who resolves his mind upon anuttara-samyak-sambodhi speaks of all dharmas as annihilated, do not think thus. Why? One who resolves his mind upon anuttara-samyak-sambodhi does not speak of the mark of annihilation.

blocks.text: Part Twenty-eight: Neither Receiving nor Coveting

inline.s: Subhuti, if a bodhisattva filled worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges with the seven treasures and used them for giving; and if another person knew that all dharmas are without self and attained the patience of non-arising, this bodhisattva’s merit would surpass the former bodhisattva’s merit. Why? Subhuti, because the bodhisattvas do not receive merit.

Subhuti addressed the Buddha: World-Honored One, how is it that a bodhisattva does not receive merit? Subhuti, the merit a bodhisattva produces should not be clung to; therefore it is said that he does not receive merit.

blocks.text: Part Twenty-nine: Dignified and Still

inline.s: Subhuti, if a person says the Tathagata comes, or goes, or sits, or lies down, that person does not understand what I have spoken. Why? ‘Tathagata’ means one who comes from nowhere and goes nowhere; therefore he is called the Tathagata.

blocks.text: Part Thirty: The Single Unified Form

inline.s: Subhuti, if good men and good women ground the three thousand great thousand worlds into particles of dust, what do you think? Would this mass of particles be many? Subhuti said: Very many, World-Honored One. Why? Because if this mass of particles truly existed, the Buddha would not have spoken of a mass of particles. How is this? What the Buddha speaks of as a mass of particles is not a mass of particles; therefore it is called a mass of particles.

World-Honored One, what the Tathagata speaks of as the three thousand great thousand worlds is not a world; therefore it is called a world. Why? If a world truly existed, it would be a union of a single mass of particles. What the Tathagata speaks of as a union of a single mass is not a union of a single mass; therefore it is called a union of a single mass.
Subhuti, that which is a union of a single mass cannot be spoken of; yet ordinary people are attached to this matter.

blocks.text: Part Thirty-one: The Non-arising of Views

inline.s: Subhuti, if a person says that the Buddha spoke of the view of self, the view of person, the view of being, and the view of lifespan, Subhuti, what do you think? Does that person understand the meaning of what I have spoken? No, World-Honored One, that person does not understand the meaning spoken by the Tathagata. Why? The World-Honored One speaks of the view of self, person, being, and lifespan as not the view of self, person, being, and lifespan; therefore they are called the view of self, person, being, and lifespan.
Subhuti, one who resolves his mind upon anuttara-samyak-sambodhi should, with regard to all dharmas, thus know, thus see, thus believe and understand, without giving rise to a mark of dharma.
Subhuti, what are called marks of dharma — the Tathagata speaks of them as not marks of dharma; therefore they are called marks of dharma.

blocks.text: The Transformation-Body Is Neither Real nor False, Chapter Thirty-Two

inline.s: Subhūti, if someone were to fill measureless asaṃkhyeya worlds with the seven treasures and give them all away in charity, while a good man or good woman who has aroused the bodhi-mind were to take up this sutra, were to take up even so much as a four-line verse of it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, and expound it for others, the merit of the latter would far surpass that of the former.
And how should one expound it for others? By not grasping at appearances, but dwelling in the suchness that does not move.
And why is this?
All conditioned things are like a dream, a phantom,
a bubble, a shadow, like dew, and like a flash of lightning.

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, the elder Subhūti, together with all the monks and nuns, the laymen and laywomen, and all the heavenly beings, humans, and asuras of every world, heard what the Buddha had said, and were filled with great joy. They believed, accepted, and reverently put it into practice.
